title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 228 (Principal not bound when excess of agent’s authority is not separable)

content.overview: Section 228 provides that where an agent does more than he is authorised to do, and what he does beyond the scope of his authority cannot be separated from what is within it, the principal is not bound to recognise the transaction. Illustration: A authorises B to buy 500 sheep; B buys 500 sheep and 200 lambs for one sum of ₹6,000 — A may repudiate the whole transaction.
content.glance: Inseparable excess of authority — principal not bound to recognise the transaction.
content.study: Where an agent does more than authorised and the excess cannot be separated from the authorised part, the principal is not bound to recognise the transaction. Illustration: A authorises B to buy 500 sheep; B buys 500 sheep and 200 lambs for one sum of ₹6,000; A may repudiate the whole transaction. Contrast s. 227, where the authorised part can be separated and only that part binds. Current-law framing: identify the excess; test separability; if inseparable, principal may repudiate the whole.

sections.heading: Excess of authority
sections.body: The agent does more than he is authorised to do.

sections.heading: Excess not separable
sections.body: What is beyond authority cannot be separated from what is within it.

sections.heading: Principal not bound
sections.body: The principal is not bound to recognise the transaction.

sections.heading: Illustration
sections.body: Authority to buy 500 sheep; agent buys sheep and lambs for one sum — principal may repudiate the whole.

provisions.title: Principal not bound when excess of agent’s authority is not separable

examples.title: Sheep and lambs for one sum
examples.body: A authorises B to buy 500 sheep. B buys 500 sheep and 200 lambs for one sum of ₹6,000. A may repudiate the whole transaction under the statutory illustration.

hypotheticals.question: If the authorised part can be separated, does s. 228 still apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Separable excess is governed by s. 227 — only the authorised part binds. Section 228 applies when the excess cannot be separated.

distinctions.title: Inseparable excess (s. 228) vs separable excess (s. 227)
distinctions.left: Principal not bound to recognise the transaction
distinctions.right: Only the authorised part binds between agent and principal

misconceptions.trap: Any excess of authority always voids the whole transaction for the principal.
misconceptions.correction: Only when the excess cannot be separated does s. 228 free the principal from recognising the transaction; separable excess is under s. 227.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 228 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the excess of authority. II. Test separability. III. If inseparable, principal not bound to recognise the transaction. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Always contrast with s. 227 on separability.
